AI video editor in Claude Code: 3 prompts, from an empty folder to a finished reel. SETUP (once) 1. Get the Claude app (claude.ai/download) and open the Code tab, not the browser. 2. Make a folder "AI Editor" with 3 folders inside: raw, references, done. 3. New chat in Code → Local → Select folder → AI Editor. Needs a paid Claude plan. PROMPT 1: TOOLS You're my video editor. We work in this folder: raw, references, done. Install and verify 5 tools: FFmpeg with libass (on Mac: ffmpeg-full, full path), faster-whisper for word-level subtitles, yt-dlp for references, Remotion, HyperFrames (npm package hyperframes). Check what's installed first. Official installs only (Homebrew, winget, npm/pip), Node.js 22+. Python packages go in a .venv here, Python 3.14 or older: pip install faster-whisper "av<19". Test each for real: burn a subtitle into a test clip, transcribe 5 seconds of audio. Show a table: tool, version, works or not. PROMPT 2: YOUR TASTE Here are reels whose editing I like: [link 1] [link 2] [link 3]. My format: [talking to camera / voiceover]. Download them with yt-dlp into references (for study only). Study each one frame by frame and by ear: pacing, shot length, pause cuts, subtitles, colors, graphics, transitions, music, the first 3 seconds. Take inspiration, but don't copy: no shots, text, logos or brand elements. Write my own style to style.md with exact values. Show it and ask what to change. PROMPT 3: EDIT My new recording is in raw. Edit it using style.md: 1. Transcribe with Whisper, word timestamps. Ask me about doubtful words before burning subtitles. 2. Cut pauses, slips and bad takes, keep the last good take. Check cut points by audio level. Keep pauses that serve the meaning, breaths and word endings. Don't speed up my voice. 3. Word-by-word subtitles in my style. 4. If references/music.mp3 exists, put it quietly under the voice. 5. Graphics only where they help. 6. Export 1080×1920 to done as draft-v1.mp4 plus edit-notes.md. Check the file yourself, then show me. I'll give edits in plain words; save each as draft-v2, draft-v3. No code words. Follow for my own editing style, coming next.

Building an app with AI? Learn these 4 parts first Want to build an app with AI? Learn the four parts first: the front end, the back end, the database, and where AI fits in a modern app. When you ask ChatGPT or Claude to build you an app (vibe coding, no code), these four parts are what you're actually describing. Explained for complete beginners. We follow one customer message through an online coffee store app, start to finish: 1. Front end: everything the customer sees and taps. The screens, the buttons, the text box. It doesn't know prices or stock. It shows things and passes messages along. 2. Back end: runs on a server the customer never sees. This is where the business rules live: login, stock, prices, payments. The front end asks, the back end decides. 3. Database: where everything is saved, like a giant spreadsheet that never closes. Products, prices, customers, orders. Only the back end opens it, and it checks who's asking. 4. AI in the middle: the back end calls the AI model only for jobs that need understanding. Job one, turn a plain sentence ("a gift for my dad, he drinks it black, under $40") into a search. Job two, write the answer using only the real products the database sent back. The rule for building reliable AI apps: AI handles the words, the back end handles the facts and the money. Never let the AI make up prices or stock. Whole app in four lines: the front end shows, the back end decides, the database remembers, the AI understands and writes. If you want to go from understanding the four parts to building your own apps with AI, I teach it step by step, from complete beginner to real systems. How to hand any job to an AI employee, start to finish (Claude Code) ow to build an AI employee in Claude Code that takes a real job off your plate, from start to finish. Done right, one job gives you back tens of hours a month. An AI employee has five parts: an agent that can take steps and use your apps, skills, memory, a schedule, and corrections. The build, on a real example (an agency's Monday client reports, 3 hours every week): 1. Write the job down like you're training a new hire, and time it. 2. Give it a desk: a folder with one job-description file Claude Code reads every time (who it is, what it owns, the rules). 3. Skills: one recipe per task (pull the numbers, write the report in your format, draft the emails). 4. Connect its hands: Google Analytics, Google Sheets, Gmail. It drafts, you approve and send. 5. Memory: a file it reads before work and writes to after. 6. Schedule: every Monday at 7 AM it does the whole job. Corrections: when it gets something wrong, fix the employee, not the output. It writes the fix into its rules. Result: 3 hours → 15 minutes. Then copy the desk for the next job. I teach it step by step, from complete beginner to running a team of AI employees.
